_readme: Concept bank for the Hamdam Instagram reel series. The agent READS this file and never writes to it. After a concept ships, set used=true by hand - and verify against live captions, because the flag has drifted before.
_weekly_structure: MONDAY hopeful and encouraging. WEDNESDAY philosophical but shared. FRIDAY always a fal, always Hafez (see fal-pool.json and make_fal_render.py). Hafez is reserved for Friday; Monday and Wednesday draw on Parvin, Rumi, Saadi and Khayyam.
_external_persian_rule: Concepts sourced from Ganjoor carry verseId 'EXTERNAL' and their own byte-exact 'persian' field plus a 'ganjoor' URL. The renderer (v11+) prefers concept['persian'] when verseId is EXTERNAL. verse-queue.json is never edited. Source: github.com/ganjoor/ganjoor-data - 240 poets, 135,319 poems over plain HTTPS.
_no_fade_rule: NEVER fade up from black when composing. Instagram ignores thumb_offset on reels and takes frame zero as the cover, so a black first frame ships a black tile in the grid and in feed - viewers scroll past before it plays. This collapsed reach on 7 and 9 September 2026 (10 and 15 accounts reached, against a 200-300 baseline). Frame zero must be the finished first page; check it measures above 25 brightness before publishing.
_english_said_rule: englishSaid is the English as a writer would say it, and page 5 shows it in preference to the queue's literal 'english'. Literal glosses are exactly the flattening this account exists to argue against.
_sendability_test: BEFORE writing a send prompt, ask WHO THE POEM POINTS AT. (a) Points at the READER'S OWN FAILING - never sendable. (b) Points at SOMETHING SHARED - sendable. (c) Points WARMLY AT THE RECIPIENT - sendable. A poem with two parties can often be rescued by pointing the prompt at the OTHER one - see rumi-022.
_cta_principle_addendum: A send prompt that DESCRIBES the recipient is an appraisal, and appraisals do not get forwarded. Strongest forms: FIRST PERSON PLURAL or SECOND PERSON - the sender adopts the line as their own words. Never accuse the reader. STRONGEST OF ALL: when the verse is itself an invitation, use the verse's own hemistich as the CTA and invent nothing - see khayyam-sh121.
_message_not_meditation: Most verses are MEDITATIONS - the poet thinking alone - and nobody forwards a meditation because there is no one it is for. The verses that get shared are already addressed to a person.
_app_link_rule: Connect a verse to the app ONLY where the connection is real. saadi-017 works because nafas is literally the dam in ham-dam.
_seasonal_note: Check the hemisphere before scheduling any verse with seasonal imagery. The audience is largely Australian diaspora.
_context_rule: Only use verses whose meaning is complete in the lines shown.
_mood_key: happy = bright Mahur; love = romantic Mahur; grave = restrained, sparse; wry = light but not celebratory.

concepts.persian:
بر نامده و گذشته بنیاد مکن
حالی خوش باش و عمر بر باد مکن
concepts.headline: DON'T BUILD ON EITHER
concepts.englishSaid: Don't build on what hasn't come or what's gone. Be well now, and don't throw a life to the wind.
concepts.argument:
Bonyad is the footing of a building. Not a metaphor for planning - the actual foundation, the part under the ground.

So Khayyam is not making a general point about time. He is watching you pour concrete into two places that are made of air, and saying: not there.

He never says seize the day. He removes the other two and lets you notice what is left standing.
concepts.insightFa: «بنیاد» یعنی پی ساختمان — خیام می‌گوید روی هوا پی نساز
concepts.insightEn: Bonyad is a building's foundation. Khayyam is saying: don't lay one on air.
concepts.lessonFa: بر آنچه نیامده و آنچه رفته، بنا نکن
concepts.lessonEn: Don't build on what hasn't come or what's gone
concepts.sendEn: Let's make the most of today
concepts._check: Persian from Ganjoor. 'pey nasaz' is Ealia's correction - you BUILD a foundation, you don't pour one. Headline was SEIZE THE MOMENT in draft and changed 11 Sep: the insight argues Khayyam never says it, so a headline saying it would contradict the reel's own point.

concepts.persian:
زمانه روشن و تاریک و گرم و سرد شود
مقام جز به سرچشمه زمانه مکن
concepts.headline: NOTHING OUT THERE HOLDS STILL
concepts.englishSaid: Time turns bright and dark, warm and cold. Seek no station except from the source of truth itself.
concepts.argument:
Four words and none of them is the point: bright, dark, warm, cold. Life going well and then badly. Rumi lists them to establish one thing - that none of it holds still.

Then maqam: station, rank, the standing you are held in. His instruction is about where to ask for it. Not from the world, whose weather you have just watched change.

Sarcheshmeh-ye zamaneh is the spring a river rises from. Rumi is pointing past time itself, to what time comes out of.
concepts.insightFa: «سرچشمهٔ زمانه» یعنی آنجا که زمان از آن جاری می‌شود
concepts.insightEn: The spring of time is where time flows from - not inside time, but before it.
concepts.lessonFa: دنیا همیشه در تغییر است؛ مقام و آرامش را از چیزهای متغیر نخواه
concepts.lessonEn: The world is always changing. Don't seek standing or peace from things that change.
concepts.sendFa: بیا آرامش را از چیزی که می‌گذرد نخواهیم
concepts.sendEn: Let's not ask for peace from what passes
concepts.poetLineFa: مولانا — بلخ و قونیه، قرن سیزدهم
concepts._check: APPROVED by Ealia 12 Sep 2026. 'Source of truth' is her resolution of the register question - see _divine_register_rule. Persian from Ganjoor.

concepts.persian:
ای دوست بیا تا غمِ فردا نخوریم
وین یک دمِ عمر را غنیمت شمریم
concepts.headline: LET'S NOT EAT TOMORROW'S SORROW
concepts.englishSaid: Friend, come - let's not eat tomorrow's sorrow. Let's count this one breath of a life as something gained.
concepts.argument:
The idiom is gham khordan - to EAT sorrow. Persian does not say you have worry; it says you consume it. Something you take in, that fills you, that you chose to put in your own mouth.

And ghanimat is a spoil of war - something taken, not something given. So the breath is not a gift you are grateful for. It is a thing you seized.

Khayyam is not offering comfort. He is proposing they do something together instead.
concepts.insightFa: خیام «غم خوردن» می‌گوید، نه «غم داشتن» — یعنی چیزی که خودت به دهان می‌بری
concepts.insightEn: Khayyam says eating sorrow, not having it. Something you put in your own mouth.
concepts.lessonFa: غم فردا را امروز نمی‌شود خورد
concepts.lessonEn: Tomorrow's sorrow can't be eaten today
concepts.sendFa: ای دوست بیا تا غمِ فردا نخوریم
concepts.sendEn: Friend, come - let's not eat tomorrow's sorrow
concepts._check: APPROVED by Ealia 9 Sep 2026. Persian from Ganjoor. The CTA IS THE VERSE'S OWN FIRST HEMISTICH - nothing invented, because 'ey dust biya' is already an invitation in the first person plural. This is the template for Wednesday. The ghanimat-as-spoils reading is interpretive and worth a native ear. SCHEDULED Wednesday 16 Sep 2026.

concepts.persian:
بر هر دو مکن تکیه که دوران فلک
در پرده هزار گونه بازی دارد
concepts.headline: COUNT ON NEITHER
concepts.englishSaid: Count on neither of the two - the turning of the sky keeps a thousand kinds of play behind the curtain.
concepts.argument:
Tekyeh kardan is to rely on - to make your plans assuming something holds. Khayyam's objection isn't that fortune is cruel. It's that it turns: dowran-e falak, the wheel going round. A thing that turns cannot be a support, whichever way it happens to be facing today.

And pardeh is the curtain in front of a stage. A thousand plays are being rehearsed behind it and you have seen none of them. You are not being punished. You are simply guessing at a plot you haven't been shown.
concepts.insightFa: «دوران فلک» یعنی چرخ می‌گردد — چیزی که می‌گردد، تکیه‌گاه نمی‌شود
concepts.insightEn: Dowran-e falak is the wheel turning. A thing that turns can't be relied on.
concepts.lessonFa: نه به خوبش دل ببند، نه از بدش بترس — هیچ‌کدام نمی‌ماند
concepts.lessonEn: Don't count on the good or fear the bad. Neither one stays.
concepts._check: APPROVED by Ealia 11 Sep 2026. Persian from Ganjoor. Her two corrections: tekyeh kardan is TO RELY ON, not to put weight on - I had turned an idiom back into its literal parts; and dowran is what makes the wheel unreliable, not merely motion. SPACING: this says almost the same thing as parvin-sh27 (neither joy nor sorrow lasts), which is held in weekday-pools.json. Do not run them in the same month.

concepts.persian:
روز بگذشت، ز خواب سحری بگذر
کاروان رفت، رهی گیر و برو، منشین
concepts.headline: THE CARAVAN HAS GONE
concepts.englishSaid: The day has gone. Leave the dawn sleep behind. The caravan has moved on - take a road, and go. Don't sit.
concepts.argument:
Four imperatives in two lines, and the last one is the only negative: manshin. Don't sit.

She isn't asking for speed. She's asking you not to stay still - which is a much lower bar, and a much harder one.

The caravan leaving is not the disaster it sounds like. The road is still there. It is only the company that has gone ahead.
concepts.insightEn: Parvin doesn't say run. She says don't sit.
concepts.lessonFa: کاروان رفته، اما راه درپیش است
concepts.lessonEn: The caravan has gone. The road is before you.
concepts.sendFa: برای تو که برای شروع، وقت را از دست ندادی
concepts.sendEn: For you, who didn't waste time getting started
concepts.poetLineFa: پروین اعتصامی — تبریز و تهران، قرن بیستم
concepts.poetLineEn: Parvin Etesami — Tabriz and Tehran, 20th century
concepts._check: Persian from Ganjoor. lessonFa and sendFa are EALIA'S WORDING 11 Sep 2026 - her CTA replaced mine, which implied the recipient had been idle; hers thanks them for an act instead. Headline is Latin-only: page 1 draws in Source Serif, which has no Arabic glyphs.

concepts.persian:
ناتوانی را به لطفی خاطر آوردن بدست
یاد عجز روزگار ناتوانی داشتن
concepts.headline: YOU WERE WEAK ONCE TOO
concepts.englishSaid: To lift someone weak with a single kindness is to remember the season when you were weak yourself.
concepts.argument:
Not charity, and not virtue. The word is yad - memory.

Parvin isn't calling kindness a duty you owe from above. She's calling it recognition: you are able to lift someone because you remember being the one on the floor.

Which makes it something you do sideways, not downwards.
concepts.insightFa: پروین لطف را وظیفه نمی‌داند — حافظه می‌داند
concepts.insightEn: Parvin doesn't call kindness a duty. She calls it memory.
concepts.lessonFa: مهربانی با ناتوان، یادآوری روزهای ناتوانی خودت است
concepts.lessonEn: Being kind to someone struggling is remembering when you struggled
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی که وقتی کم آوردی، کنارت ماند
concepts.sendEn: For the one who stayed when you had nothing left
concepts.poetLineFa: پروین اعتصامی — تبریز و تهران، قرن بیستم
concepts.poetLineEn: Parvin Etesami — Tabriz and Tehran, 20th century
concepts._check: Persian from Ganjoor. sendFa uses 'kam avordan', colloquial by choice - the account's English was criticised for sounding machine-made and the Persian should not drift the same way.

concepts.persian:
به جان مضایقه با دوستان مکن سعدی
که دوستی نبوَد هر چه ناتمام کنند
concepts.headline: NOTHING HALF-WAY IS FRIENDSHIP
concepts.englishSaid: Saadi, don't hold back from your friends. Whatever gets done half-way was never friendship.
concepts.argument:
Saadi names himself in the line - makon Saadi - and it is not gentle. He is needling himself. This is not instruction aimed at you; it is a man telling himself off for being sparing with the people he loves.

Natamam is plain: unfinished, left incomplete. Not "half-hearted", which is about feeling. Saadi is talking about what was actually done and not done.

The claim is severe if you sit with it. Not a poor friendship. Not friendship.
concepts.insightFa: سعدی به خودش طعنه می‌زند — نصیحت به خودش است، نه به تو
concepts.insightEn: Saadi is needling himself here. The advice is his own, aimed at himself, not at you.
concepts.lessonFa: کسی که نصفه نیمه کنارت باشد، دوستت نبوده
concepts.lessonEn: Someone who's only half beside you was never your friend
concepts.sendFa: برای تو که همیشه در کنارم بودی
concepts.sendEn: For you, who were always beside me
concepts._check: Persian from Ganjoor. lessonFa, sendFa and insightFa are EALIA'S OWN WORDING 9 Sep 2026 - she moved the lesson from actions to a person, made the CTA second person, and sharpened 'addresses himself' to ta'neh (needling); the English was rewritten to match her Persian rather than the reverse. OPEN QUESTION: Monday's brief is hopeful and encouraging, and this verse is a rebuke. If the register is wrong for the day, parvin-sh35 (rooz begzasht) in weekday-pools.json is the encouraging alternative. SCHEDULED Monday 14 Sep 2026.

concepts.headline: ONE GOOD BREATH
concepts.englishSaid: Once you've had one good breath with a real friend, nothing else looks like much.
concepts.argument:
The measure is nafasi - one breath. Not a year, not a friendship. One breath.

And the verb is takhayyol nakonad - does not imagine. He is not claiming other things become worthless. He is saying the mind stops picturing them.

ham-dam: the one you share that breath with. We named the app after it.
concepts.insightFa: سعدی می‌گوید «نفسی» — یک دم. و «همدم» یعنی کسی که همان دم را با تو قسمت می‌کند
concepts.insightEn: Saadi says nafasi - one breath. Hamdam means the one who shares it.
concepts.lessonFa: یک لحظهٔ خوب با دوست، بقیهٔ چیزها را کوچک می‌کند
concepts.lessonEn: One good moment with a friend makes everything else look small
concepts.sendFa: برای تویی که آن لحظه با من بودی
concepts.sendEn: For you who were there for it
concepts._check: PUBLISHED 4 Sep 2026, instagram.com/reel/Dc2aa4Ek5SM/ - reach 209, 9 likes, best like rate of any reel.

concepts.headline: TWO DAYS I REFUSE TO WORRY ABOUT
concepts.englishSaid: These two or three days of life have gone - like water down a stream, like wind across a plain. Two days have never cost me a moment's grief: the one not yet come, and the one already gone.
concepts.argument: Khayyam does not say seize the day. He names two specific days and refuses both - which leaves exactly one standing, and he never has to mention it.
concepts.insightFa: خیام نمی‌گوید «دم را دریاب» — دو روز را نام می‌برد و هر دو را کنار می‌گذارد
concepts.insightEn: Khayyam never says seize the day. He names two days and refuses both.
concepts.lessonFa: دو روز را نمی‌شود زندگی کرد: دیروز و فردا
concepts.lessonEn: Two days cannot be lived: yesterday and tomorrow
concepts.sendFa: بیا غم دیروز و فردا را نخوریم
concepts.sendEn: Let's not grieve yesterday and tomorrow
concepts._check: PUBLISHED 7 Sep 2026 by a ghost task with a black cover frame - reach 15. Do not repeat.

concepts.headline: TOMORROW IS NOT YOURS YET
concepts.englishSaid: Tomorrow is not yours to reach, and thinking of it is only fever. Don't waste this breath, even if your heart isn't burning - no one has priced what's left of your life.
concepts.argument: The word Khayyam uses is dastras - ordinary Persian for within reach. Not a philosophical term at all. So the line is practical: tomorrow is not available to you.
concepts.insightFa: «دسترس» واژهٔ روزمره است، نه فلسفی — خیام می‌گوید فردا در دسترس تو نیست
concepts.insightEn: Dastras is everyday Persian for within reach. Not a philosophical claim - a practical one.
concepts.lessonFa: فردا هنوز به دست تو نیست
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی که امروز کنارت است
concepts.sendEn: For someone who is beside you today
concepts._check: PUBLISHED 2 Sep 2026, instagram.com/reel/DcwrdcuD8Ep/ - reach 262. Corrected 9 Sep: this was previously mislabelled as khayyam-025 in the notes.

concepts.headline: THE PLAN WAS NOT MADE WITH YOU
concepts.englishSaid: Why grieve over what has to be? Why wear your soul out on useless thought? Live gladly, let the world go by in joy - the plan was made without asking you.
concepts.argument:
Khayyam is not comforting you. Read the last line again: the arrangement was made without consulting you.

If the plan was never yours to approve, then the worry you are carrying about it was never doing any work.
concepts.insightFa: خیام دلداری نمی‌دهد؛ می‌گوید تصمیم بی تو گرفته شده — و همین آزادت می‌کند
concepts.insightEn: Khayyam is not offering comfort. He says the decision was made without you - and that is what frees you.
concepts.lessonFa: بعضی چیزها را بی‌مشورت تو چیده‌اند
concepts.lessonEn: Some things were arranged without asking you
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی که با او می‌شود از نگرانی‌ها گفت
concepts.sendEn: For someone you can talk your worries through with
concepts._check: Reserve - a meditation rather than a message.

concepts.headline: LOOK DOWN ON NO ONE
concepts.englishSaid: We never thought it of him - and still we mocked him. Look down on no one.
concepts.argument:
Notice the order. Rumi does not begin with the advice - he begins by admitting that he was one of the people doing the taunting.

Advice that arrives after a confession lands differently from advice that arrives from above.
concepts.insightFa: مولانا اول اعتراف می‌کند که خودش طعنه می‌زده — نصیحت بعد از اعتراف می‌آید
concepts.insightEn: Rumi admits he did the taunting himself. The advice comes after the confession, not from above it.
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی که خوب بودنش را دیر فهمیدند
concepts.sendEn: For someone whose worth people saw too late
concepts.poetLineFa: مولانا — بلخ و قونیه، قرن سیزدهم
concepts._check: Reserve. sendFa is Ealia's wording 9 Sep 2026 - points at the person who was underestimated, not at the reader.

concepts.headline: WHY HAVE YOU FROZEN IN THAT CORNER
concepts.englishSaid: Why have you frozen in that corner? Why won't you turn too? Are you some unlucky thought that circles nothing but grief?
concepts.argument: One verb carries this line, and it repeats: to turn. Rumi is not telling you to be happy. He is pointing out that you are still moving, just in a circle of one subject.
concepts.insightFa: مولانا نمی‌گوید غم نخور؛ می‌گوید تو داری می‌گردی، اما فقط دور یک چیز
concepts.insightEn: Rumi does not say stop grieving. He says you are still turning - just around one subject.
concepts.lessonEn: Turning is easier than standing still
concepts.sendFa: چه چیزی دوباره به حرکتت می‌آورد؟
concepts.poetLineFa: مولانا — بلخ و قونیه، قرن سیزدهم

_headline_rule: headline is drawn on page 1 in Source Serif, which has NO Arabic glyphs. Latin script only - a Persian headline renders as tofu boxes. Put the Persian in the caption instead.
_spacing_note: Several Wednesday concepts make the same claim in different words - khayyam-sh84 (count on neither), parvin-sh27 (neither joy nor sorrow lasts, held in weekday-pools.json), and to a degree khayyam-sh136 and khayyam-sh121. They are individually good and collectively repetitive. Space them: never two in the same month.
_divine_register_rule: Persian mystical poetry points constantly at the divine - Rumi almost always, Hafez often. This account keeps religious framing out (poets by city and century, no God on screen), but hedging a verse into vagueness is not neutrality, it just empties it. POLICY, set by Ealia 12 Sep 2026: translate to the QUALITY the poet is pointing at, not the noun. Truth, the eternal, the source, light, wisdom, what does not change. Never 'God'. CHOOSE THE WORD FROM THE VERSE, not from a fixed list: sarcheshmeh-ye zamaneh contrasts permanence with flux, so 'the source of truth' fits (see rumi-sh2076-source); a verse built on nur would take 'light'; one on hekmat would take 'wisdom'. A believing reader and a secular one should each find their own meaning without either being misled about what the poem says.
